# ASML: valuation research and assumptions

Information cutoff: **18 October 2026**. Reporting and operating-valuation currency: **EUR**. Unless stated otherwise, financial amounts are EUR millions. All referenced public sources were reviewed by this information date.

## Result and how to use it

The coherent dated case estimates operating value of **EUR 280.842 billion** and conditional equity value of **EUR 288.099 billion**, or **EUR 745.97 per ordinary share**. The valuation origin and capital reference are **31 December 2025**, using information available through 18 October 2026. This is a retrospective updated-information research case, not a valuation that was knowable at year-end 2025 and not an October 2026 price target.

At the 31 December 2025 ECB reference exchange rate of 1.175 USD per EUR, the illustrative conversion is USD 876.52 per share. Current-price comparison is unsuitable until the operating timing, capital claims, cash and exact shares are reconciled to a common current date. No market quote or analyst target was used to select the assumptions.

ASML meets the requested US-listed security universe. The Nasdaq security is a New York registered ordinary share with one ordinary-share equivalent, quoted in USD; it is not an ADR. EUR statements are not silently converted into USD. The [issuer security description](https://investor.asml.com/share-information) and [Robinhood's official stock page](https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/ASML/) support this classification and public catalog coverage. The latter does not establish eligibility in any particular account.

## Reporting basis and historical comparability

Use US GAAP financials in EUR. Fiscal years end 31 December. The [2025 US GAAP annual report](https://ourbrand.asml.com/m/71076aaad607de4d/original/asml-2025-annual-report-based-on-us-gaap.pdf) was published 25 February 2026. Statements are on pp 276–281; revenue detail pp 286–287. The statutory 2026 interim report is IFRS: its share/debt evidence can corroborate claims, but its development-cost capitalization and earnings must not be spliced into US GAAP operating results.

The ten calendar fiscal years are not an untouched-as-originally-filed series. FY 2016–2017 use the 2018 restated revenue-recognition/lease transition comparatives. Original FY 2016 sales of EUR 6,794.8 m differ from the restated EUR 6,875.1 m. The curated data retains field-level original SEC facts and explicit manual corrections. The initial SEC taxonomy extraction did not retrieve the current-debt lines for 2016–2017 and retained older debt tags; these were corrected against the [2018 integrated report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/937966/000093796619000007/a2018integratedreportbased.htm), restated opening balance sheet and 2017 comparative balance sheet. This is why raw and curated versions remain separate.

Scope also changed: HMI was acquired in 2016; the strategic Zeiss interest in 2017; Berliner Glas in 2020, followed by disposal of non-lithography activities in 2021. The latter produced EUR 213.7 m operating disposal income. Normalized EBIT subtracts it. FY 2016 and FY 2017 normalized EBIT also excludes EUR 93.8 m and EUR 95.8 m of co-investment R&D funding other income. R&D itself remains expensed.

Company FCF is CFO less purchases of PPE and intangibles. It is not the forecast's unlevered FCFF: CFO includes financing-income effects, associate dividends, working-capital timing and customer advances; strategic supplier loans sit in investing cash flow. The accompanying historical data includes margins, taxes, R&D, compensation, balance-sheet capital and share counts. Missing early lease disclosures are treated as unknown, not zero.

## What sells, and what can grow

FY 2025 revenue consisted of EUR 11,602.7 m EUV, EUR 12,871.6 m other systems and EUR 8,193.0 m installed-base service/field options. EUV included four High-NA systems/EUR 1,156.9 m and 44 low-NA systems/EUR 10,445.8 m. DUV immersion was EUR 10,311.4 m. End-use system sales were EUR 16,054.1 m logic and EUR 8,420.2 m memory; these are an alternative classification, not an extra segment to add. China accounted for EUR 9,519.7 m, 29.1% of total revenue. Four customers each exceeded 10% and collectively represented 61.2%. These facts anchor concentration risk and prevent treating a service mix shift as four independent growth drivers. [Annual report, note 2 pp 286–287](https://ourbrand.asml.com/m/71076aaad607de4d/original/asml-2025-annual-report-based-on-us-gaap.pdf).

The primary business thesis is increased lithography intensity plus physical capacity expansion, not an extrapolation of net income. EUV and critical DUV support leading logic and DRAM/HBM transitions; upgrades raise wafer output without building a new fab. Service grows with the installed fleet and utilization, while upgrade campaigns can be unusually profitable and lumpy. High-NA adds an adoption opportunity but also acceptance, ramp-cost and substitution risks. Low-NA, High-NA and upgrade revenue must not all receive full independent growth credit for the same wafer capacity.

[Q3 2026 prepared remarks, pp 3–4](https://investor.asml.com/static-files/40c56a6b-1460-4f69-9340-6a869560d24b) describe roughly 65 low-NA systems in 2026, planned 30% capacity expansion in 2027 and exploration of more than 30% in 2028. Orders, interest in future orders, factory capacity, shipments and recognized revenue are different quantities. The forecast does not translate every capacity percentage one-for-one into sales growth.

[The executive video interview, pp 2–4](https://investor.asml.com/static-files/7ec38683-352c-4cc9-923e-c2af8199e876) places the pricing benefit partly in 2027 and fully in 2028 and beyond. The NXE:3800F and higher-throughput immersion tools should improve customer economics. Management reports Samsung/TSMC High-NA adoption plans for 2028/2030; these are company-described customer intentions, not independently guaranteed deliveries.

The [July prepared call remarks](https://ourbrand.asml.com/asset/1fd3908a-0381-47b5-9b69-a3094f656651/2026_07_15-ASML-Transcript-investor-call-Q2-2026.pdf) and executive interview were also reviewed. The full October Q&A was read in a [secondary transcription](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/14/asml-asml-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). It corroborates the importance of customer fab readiness, ramp costs and non-recurring upgrade campaigns; numbers are governed by primary disclosures because the transcription contains errors. The official PDF labelled investor-call transcript contains prepared remarks, not a full Q&A transcript. This limitation is preserved rather than claiming all Q&A was primary.

## Latest period, extraordinary income, and cash

The latest reported quarter ended 27 September 2026, not 30 September. Nine-month revenue was EUR 29,755.4 m and EBIT EUR 11,786.8 m. Q3 revenue was EUR 11,662.0 m and EBIT EUR 5,172.8 m. Derived TTM revenue is EUR 39,473.5 m and EBIT EUR 15,217.7 m, using FY 2025 plus current nine months less the matching prior nine months. [Q3 SEC financial statements, statements of operations and quarterly summary](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/937966/000162828026065813/financial_statementsxusx.htm).

The Q3 EUR 509.7 m equity-investment gain is below operating income. It is excluded from operating forecasts; adding the investment's value separately must not capitalize that gain a second time. Equity-investment holdings of EUR 2,239.4 m are not assumed to be all Mistral. [Q3 financial statements, operations and balance sheet](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/937966/000162828026065813/financial_statementsxusx.htm).

Quarterly CFO was EUR 11,797.6 m and company FCF EUR 11,350.4 m, with a EUR 7,009.0 m cash contribution from changes in assets/liabilities. Noncurrent contract liabilities jumped from EUR 3,570.3 m to EUR 9,300.6 m. The earnings call attributes strong cash generation to order-related downpayments. Neither Q3 FCF nor the Q3 net-income margin is annualized in this case.

## Bookings conversion and customer financing

The January 2026 release gives FY 2025 net bookings EUR 28,035 m and year-end system backlog EUR 38,797 m, compared with EUR 18,899 m/EUR 35,938 m in 2024. Booking/backlog definitions include accepted written system orders and inflation adjustments. Backlog excludes already recognized sales; installed-base sales are a separate revenue stream. Simple backlog-to-total-revenue division is not a delivery forecast. [FY 2025 release p 1 and footnotes 2–4](https://investor.asml.com/static-files/cb0839f6-8180-4c98-ba1a-a43348c3421d).

The audited contract note supplies a more useful, but different, measure: remaining performance obligations were EUR 46.5 bn at FY 2025, with 65% expected within twelve months, versus EUR 43.3 bn/59% one year earlier. RPO includes contractual obligations beyond the systems-backlog scope. Opening contract-liability revenue recognition was EUR 11,516.6 m in 2025 against EUR 18,196.2 m opening liabilities, about 63.3%; 2024 was EUR 9,047.5 m against EUR 16,266.5 m, about 55.6%. These are contract-liability conversion ratios, not backlog-conversion ratios. [Annual report note 2 pp 286–287](https://ourbrand.asml.com/m/71076aaad607de4d/original/asml-2025-annual-report-based-on-us-gaap.pdf).

Do not invent a numerical Q3 2026 booking total from management's order-momentum language or from the downpayment movement. Customer acceptance, fast shipments, delivery rescheduling and export licenses can shift recognized revenue; facilities must be ready to take the tools. The 2022 fast-shipment deferral into 2023 is a concrete example. The model therefore uses conservative positive incremental working-capital funding rather than extrapolating permanent advance-driven negative capital. The customer-advance stress below adds funding runoff and does not automatically assume a cash release when sales fall.

## Guidance reliability

Original dated guidance is compared with actual results below. The separate evidence schedule preserves release dates, primary links and locators.

- FY 2022 initial January 19 outlook: about 20% revenue growth. Actual 13.77%. AboutEUR 3.1 bn of fast shipments deferred recognition into 2023.
- FY 2023 January 25 outlook: growth above 25%, slight gross-margin improvement. Actual 30.15%, gross margin 51.3% versus 50.5%.
- FY 2024 first outlook on October 18 2023: revenue similar to 2023. Actual+2.56%. “Similar” has no explicit statistical tolerance.
- FY 2025 October 15 2024 annual range: EUR 30–35 bn and 51–53% gross margin. ActualEUR 32.667 bn/52.8% fell inside. The older November 2022 scenario, however, had 54–56% margin: actual missed its lower bound by 1.2 points. A near-term beat does not erase a long-range miss.
- FY 2026 original January 28 range: EUR 34–39 bn and 51–53% margin. Revisions were EUR 36–40 bn inApril, EUR 43–45 bn/54–56% inJuly, and EUR 44–45 bn/~56% inOctober. FY 2026 is unfinished; the latest estimate is not an actual-result score.
- 2026 Q1 revenue was within guidance. Q2 exceeded the revenue high end byEUR 326.5 m and the margin high end by 2 points. Q3 was within revenue guidance but 0.5 points above its margin high end, helped by upgrades.

These four finished annual observations and three current-year quarters are a limited calibration set, not a statistically estimated management-hit probability. Retain broad distributions, correlate growth/margin/reinvestment, and retain a downcycle path. The 2024 Capital Markets Day EUR 44–60 bn/56–60% 2030 opportunity is a dated scenario, not a hard ceiling. [Original 2030 update](https://investor.asml.com/news-releases/news-release-details/asml-provides-updated-view-market-opportunities-2024-investor-day-meeting).

## Dated forecast and investment case

The FY 2026 unadjusted operating estimate combines reported nine months with the midpoint of Q4 management guidance: revenue of 29,755.4 + 14,700 = 44,455.4, and EBIT of 11,786.8 + 14,700 × 57% − 1,200 − 400 = 18,565.8. The management source is the [14 October prepared earnings remarks, page 2](https://investor.asml.com/static-files/40c56a6b-1460-4f69-9340-6a869560d24b), alongside the [official Q3 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/937966/000162828026065813/pressreleasefinancialresul.htm). Economic compensation adjustments described below then reduce operating income.

The analyst segment allocation for 2026 is EUV 17.0 bn, other systems 15.2173 bn and installed-base service/field options 12.2381 bn. Installed-base revenue combines reported nine months with guided Q4. EUV is consistent with management's greater-than-45% growth indication; other systems is the residual. These are linked classifications, not independent opportunities to double-count customer spending.

For 2027, EUV, other systems and installed-base growth are 25%, 10% and 12%. For 2028, they are 20%, 10% and 10%; for 2029, 12%, 6% and 8%; for 2030, 10%, 5% and 6%. Total revenue reaches 69.17 bn in 2030, above the older 60 bn scenario. This is an explicit analyst judgment based on the much higher 2026 anchor and capacity plans, not a newly announced formal 2030 company target. Growth then fades to 2.5% by 2035.

Margins reflect productivity, pricing and mix benefits, followed by normalization as capacity costs, High-NA adoption and R&D persist. They are economic margins after future grant cost, with residual non-compensation costs held fixed when that grant budget is sensitized. R&D remains fully expensed.

Reinvestment covers PPE and intangible purchases less operating D&A, positive working-capital funding and net strategic supplier financing. FY 2026 uses 1,900 PPE + 180 intangible capex − 1,050 D&A + 15% of incremental revenue + 600 supplier funding. The result is 3,398.215. Through 2032, gross capex ratios of 5.5% initially fade toward 4.5%; D&A is 2.3–2.5% of sales; working-capital investment is 15% of incremental sales, without automatic release in a decline; supplier funding fades from 1% toward 0.5% of sales. The 2033–2035 transition then converges to the terminal capital-efficiency policy.

Strategic loans and advances are an economic cost of supply capacity even when classified outside operating cash flow. FY 2025 Zeiss loans of 1,907.5 and advances of 1,191.9 make a zero supplier-funding assumption implausible. Historical cash-flow depreciation/addbacks include debt amortization and discounted-loan accretion, so operating D&A is specified separately. The precise future funding ratios remain estimates.

Tax is 17% through 2028 and rises to 25.8%. This does not assume perpetual renewal of the 2024–2028 innovation-box agreement. Terminal ROIC of 25% is substantially below the exceptionally high unadjusted accounting return generated by customer funding and expensed research. A five-year R&D capitalization diagnostic lowers FY 2025 return to about 47.7%; that diagnostic asset is not also added to the base investment model.

### Discount rate

Cash flows and discount rates are nominal EUR. The [Bundesbank ten-year benchmark](https://api.statistiken.bundesbank.de/rest/data/BBSSY/D.REN.EUR.A630.000000WT1010.A?format=csv&lang=en) was 3.42% on 16 October 2026. The [October 1 implied equity-risk premium](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/home.htm) was 4.20% over the quoted US Treasury, with a 0.22% stated default-spread adjustment: 4.42% on a default-free reference. The [January 2026 semiconductor-equipment data](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/datafile/Betas.html) provides a 1.39 cash-adjusted unlevered beta from 31 US firms, a peer proxy rather than ASML's observed current regression beta.

A 0.50 percentage-point risk overlay, 0.5% target debt weight and 4.42% pretax borrowing-cost assumption produce roughly 10.06% WACC, rounded to 10%. These are visible analyst choices. Terminal 8% WACC assumes mature beta near one and a smaller overlay; it is not a prediction that the risk-free rate must fall. WACC remains above the 2.5% perpetual growth rate.

## Compensation and ownership

The economic cost of new grants is not the same as reported amortized compensation expense. [Annual-report note 20, pp 303–305](https://ourbrand.asml.com/m/71076aaad607de4d/original/asml-2025-annual-report-based-on-us-gaap.pdf) supplies 2025 new conditional grants:
-261,198 EUR-denominated grants at EUR 636.49 weighted average grant-date value: EUR 166.250 m
-279,674 USD-denominated grants at USD 660.67: USD 184.772 m

The 255 published 2025 [ECB daily USD/EUR observations](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist.xml) average 1.1299831373. Dividing the aggregate USD grant value by that mean gives a EUR 163.518 m proxy. Total gross grant value isEUR 329.768 m, or 1.009473% ofFY 2025 sales. Exact grant-date FX is unavailable in this aggregate table; annual-average conversion is explicitly a proxy. No forfeiture credit is assumed.

This ratio is the future economic grant-cost budget. Future dilution is not then separately charged for those grants. Residual operating costs include D&A and cash employee purchase-plan retention bonuses.

For 2026, replace the annualized nine-month reported SBC estimate,162.8×4/3=217.067, inside the management-derived EBIT anchor with the economic grant budget. This lowers economic operating income; it does not add value by removing all employee compensation. Nine-month SBC is reported; the annualization is an explicit estimate of the missing Q4 amortized amount.

For 2027 onward and terminal, replace the old 2025 amortized-SBC ratio with the economic-grant ratio, holding all other cost ratios fixed. Each affected margin falls by about 0.3902 percentage points relative to the initial amortized-expense margin calibration. The mature economic margin becomes about 39.61% instead of 40%. Grant-cost sensitivity changes only the grant budget while holding residual non-SBC costs and explicit-period investment amounts fixed. Terminal reinvestment changes with NOPAT under the growth/ROIC formula.

Existing conditional awards are treated separately. The issuer reports EUR 215 m of remaining expense over a weighted-average 1.4 years. A synthetic GAAP-like bridge deducts 153.571 m in 2026 and 61.429 m in 2027 and reverses exactly the same amounts in the same years. This creates zero uplift above the economic margins. The matching 0.778707 m legacy award count is allocated separately. The aggregate recognition timing is an assumption, but it has no valuation effect because deduction and reversal cancel within each period. Performance-based vesting remains a conditional-count allocation rather than an independently priced grant appraisal. These shares have no dividend entitlement while vesting, so no extra dividend accrual is added.

The 10,122 old options were fully exercisable and have no future compensation expense to reverse. Full-share allocation with no exercise-proceeds credit is deliberately conservative. Forgone exercise proceeds are only approximately EUR 0.870 m using the dated 1.175 FX; this is disclosed rather than called an exact option valuation.

## Opening taxes and claims

The annual capital bridge uses these identifiable claims:
- Bonds: disclosed 31 December 2025 market valueEUR 3,590.8 m
- Commercial paper: EUR 691.7 m carrying proxy
- Berliner Glas mortgage: EUR 16.4 m carrying proxy
- Finance lease: EUR 16.5 m, separately identified within accrued liabilities
- Net interest-rate swap liability:48.1−0.2=EUR 47.9 m
- Opening current tax liability 486.6 plus noncurrent tax liability 183.0: EUR 669.6 m
- Opening current tax asset: EUR 88.9 m credit, giving a EUR 580.7 m net opening tax claim

Debt market proxy and funded-debt book value are alternatives, never cumulative. The 57.5 bond carrying-value hedge adjustment is not confused with 47.9 net swap fair value. Operating leases stay within rent expense. FX derivatives retain operating treatment.

Noncurrent tax liabilities include 174.5 of uncertain tax benefits/interest/penalties and 8.5 of deferred tax. Future normalized tax rates apply to future operating profits; they do not discharge these opening balances. Those opening settlements are therefore deducted once here and excluded from future working-capital/tax cash-flow assumptions. Noncurrent deferred tax assets of 1,719.4 receive zero separate credit to avoid capitalizing tax advantages already reflected in effective-rate assumptions. Liability settlement timing and asset recovery remain disclosed proxies.

Cash and short investments total 13,321.9. A 3,000 analyst operating-liquidity reserve leaves 10,321.9 of conditional surplus. Private equity receives a 20% haircut to its 1,320.7 book value, leaving a 1,056.56 asset credit. Zeiss ownership uses 822.6 book value as a separate proxy because its profit/dividends are excluded from operating EBIT; strategic supplier loans/advances are not added to surplus cash. These are transparent valuation judgments, not claims of independently appraised fair value.

## Customer advances

Opening advances total 19,372.6. The base holds this balance constant nominally during the explicit forecast. Each year's release against delivery is replaced with equal new advances from new orders. The model therefore receives no extra cash benefit from growth in advances. This replacement assumption, not a second collection of previously prepaid revenue, supports the normalized revenue-to-cash relationship.

Positive 15%incremental working-capital investment excludes advance-growth credit. If replacement receipts fail, advance runoff is added to working-capital investment, not deducted again as debt:
-50% of opening advances runs off evenly over five years: operating value fallsEUR 7.344 bn
-100% runoff over five years: operating value fallsEUR 14.687 bn

These isolate funding dependence with revenue/margins unchanged; a true business downturn could combine runoff with lower sales and margins. The 3 bn liquidity reserve does not replace this runoff analysis. Terminal reinvestment at 10%ofNOPAT covers total net operating capital with no additional advance-growth windfall.

## Terminal continuity

The final 2035 year reaches 2.5% revenue growth, the revised 39.61% economic operating margin,25.8%tax and 8%WACC. Investment transitions over 2033–2035 to 10%ofNOPAT, consistent with 2.5%terminal growth divided by 25%ROIC. The additional/released capital is shown explicitly beside the original component model. Terminal FCFF grows exactly 2.5% from the final explicit year. The endpoint is not repaired by hiding a higher terminal multiple.

## Current-date limits and practical interpretation

The dated annual capital basis is coherent; a current basis has material public-data gaps. The audited 31 December 2025 count is 385,417,665 outstanding ordinary shares, plus 2,730,009 treasury shares, equal to 388,147,674 issued. The standalone issuer webpage transposes two labels; the annual report and its footnote resolve the discrepancy. The [2026 AGM record-date disclosure](https://www.asml.com/en/company/governance/shareholders/shareholder-meetings/agm-2026) gives 384,923,645 outstanding on 25 March. The June interim number is rounded, and Q3 weighted-average shares are earnings denominators rather than exact outstanding shares.

The September 27 balance sheet provides cash and short investments of 12,735.1 and noncurrent debt of 1,963.0, but current liabilities are aggregated. Announced buybacks cannot establish current cash or shares without settlement, employee issuance and other spending. The public Euronext index also identifies an October 8 capital increase. An exact October share/cash figure therefore cannot be manufactured from the available repurchase totals.

A separate October 18 operating-only scenario uses an explicit remaining-quarter cash-flow forecast and a 74/95-day timing convention. Its equity and current share outputs are left unknown. It is not a substitute for the dated conditional case or a verified current capital bridge.

The private-investment haircut, operating-cash reserve, tax recovery, award vesting and customer-advance replacement are valuation choices rather than undiscovered accounting facts. They should remain adjustable and stress-tested. A true adverse business scenario could combine lower sales, weaker margins, higher risk and customer-funding runoff; the isolated runoff tests above do not capture all of those effects at once.

The useful conclusion is a transparent research valuation with a defensible EUR operating model, explicit shareholder claims and preserved uncertainty. It is not a recommendation to trade or a guarantee of realized value.
